walkthroughs.body_html:
Development of Practical Skills — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Development of Practical Skills brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Development of Practical Skills.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.

mcqs.q: Why are X-linked recessive conditions more common in males?
options: Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
X-linked recessive conditions affect more males because the Y chromosome makes the disease worse.
Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed — there's no second X to mask it.
X-linked conditions affect only males because females cannot inherit X-linked alleles.

mcqs.q: Why is interspecific competition between similar species important?
options: Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.
Competition only happens between predators and their prey.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Two species cannot occupy exactly the same niche indefinitely — competition often leads to displacement or niche divergence.
